task_message:
Case L27: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 221x221x176 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case L27 complete. Summary of what I did:

- **Finding the lesion:** Overview and multi-plane contact sheets showed a large, fat-containing (lipomatous) mass in the anterior compartment of one thigh, extending roughly 14 cm cranio-caudally, with a brighter fatty periphery and a more streaky/heterogeneous core.
- **Seeding:** A single positive point in the mass core on axial ~100 gave an initial mask (v1, 496 mL) that captured the core but missed the fatty periphery and the distal portion.
- **Correction:** Positive points in the distal fatty component (axial 168) extended the mask to the distal volume edge (v2, 698 mL); `seg_refine` cleaned the boundary (v3, 692 mL).
- **Verification:** Checked the mask against the image on axial slices 24, 36, 44, 80, 99, 130, 172, 175 and coronal/sagittal views; the green outline follows the visible capsule of the encapsulated mass, bounding it against the surrounding muscles and subcutaneous fat.
- **Candidates:** All five automatic candidates were ring-like peripheral fat/subcutaneous fat or tiny slivers outside the capsule — all rejected as normal tissue.
- **Final:** Single connected component, 691.6 mL, extent axial 33–175, saved with medium confidence (some residual uncertainty at the extreme ends and at the fatty periphery vs. adjacent intermuscular fat).
